Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/QEMU (QEMU fork). SIMPLIFICATION + EFFICIENCY code-quality review. REPORT ONLY — do not edit.

Scope: STAGED change in hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c. Get it with `git diff --cached`. It replaces a local `memory_region_init_ram` + add_subregion with the `machine->ram` idiom and adds a 6-line explanatory comment.

EFFICIENCY: init-time code, 8 lines — almost certainly nothing. Only flag if real.

SIMPLIFICATION:
- The new comment is 6 lines explaining the memory-backend-file capability. Is that the right amount, or verbose? Compare with the comment density of nearby code in the same function and how hw/riscv/virt.c comments its machine->ram usage (it likely has little/no comment). Recommend tightening ONLY if it's genuinely over-long for the convention; a comment documenting non-obvious behavior (the -object memory-backend-file capability) is legitimately worth keeping.
- Any other redundancy introduced by the diff.
For each finding: file, line, summary, simpler form. Behavior-preserving only. If clean, say so. Be concise.

content.text:
Diff is clean. No efficiency issues, no redundancy. One optional simplification on comment length.

## EFFICIENCY
Nothing. The change removes a heap allocation (`g_new(MemoryRegion, 1)`) and a `memory_region_init_ram` call, replacing them with the pre-built `machine->ram`. Strictly less init-time work, and the new `default_ram_id` line is required boilerplate for the idiom.

## SIMPLIFICATION

**Finding 1 (optional): `hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c:1363-1368` — comment is verbose relative to local + sibling convention.**

The diff replaces the original 1-line `/* register system main memory (actual RAM) */` with a 6-line block. Nearby comments in the same function are all single-line tags (`/* NOR FLASH */`, `/* HVM */`, `/* boot rom */`). The sibling machine `virt.c:1597` documents the identical `machine->ram` line with a bare `/* register system main memory (actual RAM) */` and no explanation at all.

That said, the comment documents genuinely non-obvious behavior (the `-object memory-backend-file` capability and the default-backend equivalence), which is legitimately worth keeping per your own criterion. The verbosity is in the *example invocation* and the redundant reassurance, not the core point. A 3-line version preserves the load-bearing facts (where RAM comes from + default equivalence) and drops the inline CLI tutorial:

```c
    /* register system main memory (actual RAM); machine->ram lets
     * -machine ...,memory-backend=<id> map DRAM onto a user backend
     * (e.g. memory-backend-file), else an anonymous one is auto-created. */
```

This is a judgment call, not a defect. Keeping the 6 lines is defensible since the behavior is non-obvious. Recommend trimming only if matching local single-purpose-comment density matters to you; the content itself is correct and worth documenting.

No other redundancy. The removal of `main_mem` and its allocation is complete and clean — no dangling references.
